Man dies in Bas-Uele after travelling from Haut-Uele, as head of WHO says outbreak on track to be deadliest ever

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has spread to a sixth province, officials have said, a day after the head of the World Health Organization said the outbreak was on track to surpass the deadliest in history, which killed at least 11,000 people more than a decade ago.

guardian.description:
Disciplinary proceedings under way after security concerns raised over reported visits to official residence

France has opened disciplinary proceedings against its ambassador to Central African Republic over allegations of misconduct, after claims he brought dozens of women into his official residence, raising potential security concerns.

guardian.title: Zambia elections haunted by ghost of incumbent president’s arch-rival
guardian.description:
Hakainde Hichilema is bidding for second term, but feud between him and family of Edgar Lungu, who died in 2025, continues

As Zambians go to the polls on Thursday, the ghost of the current president’s predecessor hangs over the elections.

Hakainde Hichilema, 64, is bidding for a second term leading the southern African country after defeating his arch-rival Edgar Lungu by a landslide in 2021.

guardian.title: At least 44 dead after overcrowded ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe
guardian.description:
Operation under way to rescue dozens missing after boat overturned by waves at world’s largest human-made lake

At least 44 people have died after an overcrowded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, police said.

The boat had a capacity of 90 people, but was carrying 114 adult passengers, five crew members and an unknown number of children, Zimbabwe’s civil protection unit (CPU) said earlier on Wednesday, citing ticket sales.

guardian.description:
South African scientist’s breakthrough research shows soil fungus could be used in fight against devastating crop pest

Hearing about fields full of dead caterpillars enveloped in a mysterious white substance intrigued the South African scientist Letodi Luki Mathulwe. Something was killing off the African armyworm – one of the most devastating pests for farmers in east and southern Africa.

Ángel Aguirre indicted in case that rocked Mexico and became symbol of its brutal cartel violence

guardian.description:
Female staff alleged company failed to maintain safe workplace, after allegations of sexual assault against pilot

The Canadian airline WestJet has agreed to pay C$4.5m (£2.4m) to settle a decade-long sexual harassment class action lawsuit levelled by its female flight attendants, who alleged the company failed to maintain a safe workplace.

guardian.title: Canadian airline cancels flight after child refuses to wear seatbelt
guardian.description:
Flight from Victoria to Toronto forced to return to terminal after repeated attempts to secure child in seat failed

A Canadian airline cancelled a flight from Victoria to Toronto after a child refused to wear a seatbelt.

guardian.title: Scores dead in Colombia after powerful earthquake strikes west of country
guardian.description:
Quake of 7.4 magnitude collapses and severely damages buildings in several major cities, including Cali and Pereira

More than 100 people died after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, collapsing and severely damaging scores of buildings in major cities including Cali and Pereira.

guardian.title: ‘Absolutely unacceptable’: Japan condemns visit by Vladimir Putin to disputed Kuril Islands
guardian.description:
Japanese PM says islands seized by Soviets late in second world war are part of her country under international law

The Japanese government has reacted angrily to Vladimir Putin’s first visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, which are claimed by both Tokyo and Moscow.

Japan’s foreign minister, Toshimitsu Motegi, summoned the Russian ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev, while the prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, called Putin’s actions “absolutely unacceptable”.

guardian.title: South Korean airport becomes busiest in world for global traffic amid Iran war
guardian.description:
Incheon airport had 38.39m international passengers in first half of 2026, as traffic diverted from Middle East hubs

South Korea’s Incheon airport has become the world’s busiest airport for international passengers, in part owing to disruption in the Middle East caused by the Iran war.

guardian.description:
Prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul calls for tighter gun controls and ‘decisive penalties’ after nine dead in school shooting

Thailand has suspended firearms licences after the deadly Nonthaburi school shooting, as the bodies of the teenage attacker and the grandparents he killed were cremated.

Thousands of people have been evacuated from areas at risk of flooding and landslides in Beijing, as the remnants of Typhoon Dolphin continue to bring torrential rain to northern and central China.

guardian.title: Passenger jet billed as China’s answer to Boeing and Airbus prepares to make first international flight
guardian.description:
The Comac C919 will fly from Beijing to Ulaanbaatar in Mongolia, although experts say it could take generations for it to challenge the west’s dominance of the industry

China hopes to break into the world of commercial aviation with the first international flight of a Chinese-made passenger jet scheduled for Wednesday.

The Comac C919 will take off from Beijing capital international airport at 3pm, landing in Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia, just over two hours later.

rfi.title: France and 30 other countries condemn Iran's executions of protestors
rfi.description: More than 30 countries, including France, the United Kingdom and Canada, have condemned Iran's use of capital punishment, saying in a joint statement on Wednesday the Islamic Republic was executing protesters to "silence dissent". Tehran accused its critics of hypocrisy.

rfi.title: Romania shuts down nuclear plant due to low level of drought-hit Danube
rfi.description: Romania on Thursday began a complete shutdown of its only nuclear plant after levels of water in the River Danube – used to cool the site – fell to a record low, the national nuclear energy company said.

rfi.title: Morocco steps up border security over fears of new mass crossing into Ceuta
rfi.description: Morocco has stepped up security along its borders with the Spanish enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla after fresh calls appeared on social media urging migrants to attempt another mass crossing, weeks after tens of thousands rushed the frontier.

rfi.title: Sister act ushers underdogs Malawi into WAFCON final against Cameroon
rfi.description: Goals from sisters Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga on Wednesday gave tournament outsiders Malawi a 3-1 victory over Algeria, sending them to the Women's Africa Cup of Nations final – after they qualified for the tournament for the first time this year.

rfi.title: Voters in Zambia to deliver verdict on president's economic record
rfi.description: Zambia are voting in a general election on Thursday which will decide whether President Hakainde Hichilema returns for a second term, after steering the country out of a debt crisis.

rfi.title: Can UK's hard-right Farage bin financial probe with by-election win?
rfi.description: Nigel Farage – leader of the anti-immigration Reform UK party – will be fighting for his parliamentary seat on Thursday, going head to head with parody candidate Count Binface in snap polls. The by-election was called after Farage resigned amid a probe into his finances. But the surprise move threatens to backfire as none of the major political parties has fielded a candidate.

rfi.title: Russia threatens retaliatory seizures of EU ships amid new sanctions push
rfi.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday threatened to seize ships belonging to European countries in retaliation for plans to sell off cargo seized from Russian "shadow fleet" vessels.

rfi.title: French ambassador to CAR disciplined over misconduct allegations
rfi.description: France’s foreign ministry has launched disciplinary proceedings against its ambassador to the Central African Republic, following allegations that he repeatedly brought young women to the official residence in Bangui and had sexual relations with some of them.

rfi.title: Millions gather to watch as solar eclipse plunges swathe of Spain into darkness
rfi.description: Millions of spectators – tourists and locals alike – gathered in parks and cities across Spain to see Wednesday's total solar eclipse, the first of its kind in the country in more than a century.

rfi.title: France gripped by latest summer heatwave as drought conditions worsen
rfi.description: Scorching heat continued to spread across most of mainland France on Wednesday, as the Ministry for Ecological Transition met to take stock of the effects of a drought that has been steadily worsening since May.

rfi.title: Hungary elects Orban critic Andras Baka as first president in new political era
rfi.description: Hungarian lawmakers on Tuesday approved former supreme court chief Andras Baka – a prominent critic of Viktor Orban who was ousted during the ex-premier's time in power – as the country's next head of state.

rfi.title: Assisted dying, social media and agriculture put France’s top court in spotlight
rfi.description: France’s Constitutional Council is facing a politically charged end to the summer, with judges due to rule on a series of high-profile laws – including those covering assisted dying, social media use by children, agriculture and public security.

rfi.title: Lebanon becomes first country in Middle East to abolish death penalty
rfi.description: Lebanon’s parliament on Tuesday abolished the death penalty, making it the first country in the Middle East to replace capital punishment with a sentence of life imprisonment with hard labour.

rfi.title: Former Syrian leader Assad sentenced to death in absentia over war crimes
rfi.description: A Syrian court on Tuesday sentenced former ruler Bashar al-Assad to death after a trial in absentia, convicting him of atrocities committed during the country's civil war. Six of his closest aides were also handed death sentences.

rfi.title: Race to find Ebola vaccine as DR Congo outbreak kills more than 2,000
rfi.description: The latest outbreak of Ebola has killed more than 2,000 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to health authorities. Meanwhile, international efforts have been stepped up to test a vaccine for the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever.

rfi.title: France and EU join international aid effort after Colombia earthquake
rfi.description: France has joined the European Union and a host of countries in offering assistance to Colombia, where volunteers and rescuers are searching for survivors following Monday's deadly earthquake.

rfi.title: May ’68 protest leader Cohn-Bendit pledges support to Glucksmann for 2027
rfi.description: Former Green MEP Daniel Cohn-Bendit, a historic figure on the French left, on Monday gave his support to Raphaël Glucksmann for France’s 2027 presidential election, in an interview with Le Point magazine.

rfi.title: Rebel forces in Ethiopia's Tigray state condemn army drone strikes
rfi.description: Rebel authorities on Tuesday accused the Ethiopian government of carrying out deadly drone strikes in southern Tigray state and condemned the move as "a serious escalation", amid fears of a new war.

euronews.title: Víctor Coyote dies: a life impossible to confine to music, comics and film
euronews.description: Víctor Coyote, stage name of Víctor María Aparicio Abundancia, died on Thursday in Galicia in a cycling accident. He was 67 and left behind a four-decade career spanning music, comics, film and music videos.

euronews.title: Survivors tell of horror of Zimbabwe ferry sinking as police say death toll hits 46
euronews.description: The overloaded government ferry, a vital link for villagers and fish traders around the vast Lake Kariba, overturned in choppy waters on Tuesday in one of the country's worst passenger boat disasters.

euronews.title: Explosion rocks ammunition factory near Rome, Italian police say
euronews.description: Italian media reported that there were no casualties, with the AGI news agency saying employees sheltered in secure areas at the facility.

euronews.title: Etna eruption enters seventh day in phenomenon unseen since the 1970s
euronews.description: Euronews has gathered the views of experts and local guides on the unusual length of the eruption and on the precautions to take to watch it safely.

euronews.title: Latest news bulletin | August 13th, 2026 – Evening
euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this August 13th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: In Paris, tourists increasingly choose cycling to explore the city
euronews.description: On Paris's streets, bicycles are increasingly common, and tourists play a big part. Guided bike tours have boomed in recent years.

euronews.title: Ukraine needs 5% of US Patriot stocks just to get through winter, Zelenskyy says
euronews.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv currently receives only 1% of the interceptor missiles it needs from Washington, as Russian strikes continue to outpace the country's air defences.

euronews.title: Hundreds of tourists rescued by boat as forest fire threatens northern Greek beaches
euronews.description: A fire service spokesman said the evacuation had to be by sea as the flames were getting close to the beaches.

euronews.title: One dead, several injured in Rotterdam port blast at Gunvor refinery
euronews.description: The Netherlands is investigating an explosion at the port of Rotterdam that killed one person and injured several others on Thursday, 13 August. The blast happened at about 11:30 a.m. at an oil facility in the Europoort industrial section of Europe’s largest port.

euronews.title: Bomb hidden in bin kills Russian officer in occupied Sevastopol, Moscow says
euronews.description: Media reports named the dead man as a Ukrainian navy defector who went on to command a Kalibr missile submarine for Moscow's Black Sea Fleet.

euronews.title: Brussels unveils giant flower carpet inspired by Hokusai masterpiece
euronews.description: Brussels has transformed its historic Grand Place into a giant floral version of Japan’s Great Wave off Kanagawa, using around 500,000 dahlias laid out over 1,300 square metres of cobblestones.

euronews.title: Poland thwarts unprecedented plot by Russia to kill Ukrainian-US citizen in a NATO country, PM Tusk says
euronews.description: Poland, a NATO and EU member state along the alliance's Eastern flank, has accused Russia of "sabotage" on several occasions since Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

euronews.title: These are Europe’s best-value cities for a weekend break - and Poland dominates the top five
euronews.description: A new study has revealed the best-value European cities for a weekend away, with Polish destinations sweeping the top five and some of the continent’s biggest tourist hotspots proving much pricier.

euronews.title: Explosion at Dutch port of Rotterdam leaves one dead and several injured, police say
euronews.description: The explosion happened at a refinery and fuel terminal run by Gunvor Energy in an industrial section of the vast port premises.

euronews.title: Hungary unveils new 'clean up' plan as governemnt takes new steps to unlocking frozen EU funds
euronews.description: Budapest will keep a list of economic operators who are barred from public tenders due to prior economic offences, fulfilling an EU obligation to restoring its access to critical funding.

euronews.title: Byway launches free online course to help you plan out a rail trip across Europe
euronews.description: The course covers things like how to choose the right Interrail pass and how to manage disruptions.

euronews.title: Iran's military rejects Trump's claims of US control over Strait of Hormuz as 'lies'
euronews.description: Iran has kept control of Hormuz, a vital energy conduit, since the outbreak of the war on 28 February, requiring vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the waterway.

euronews.title: Trump’s vaccine overhaul could fuel mistrust and leave Europe vulnerable to disease resurgence
euronews.description: The fallout from US President Donald Trump’s executive order aimed at reducing the number of universally recommended childhood immunisations could extend beyond the United States, fuelling vaccine mistrust and creating immunisation gaps.

lemonde.title: « Juillet et août étaient les mois de la légèreté » : quand la répétition des canicules chasse l’insouciance estivale
lemonde.description: La canicule se poursuit en France, avec la quasi-totalité du pays placée en vigilance orange, jeudi. La répétition des vagues de chaleur pèse sur le moral, comme le racontent les habitants du Perreux et de Nogent-sur-Marne, en région parisienne.

lemonde.title: Les ménages solos, toujours plus nombreux, peinent à se loger : « Avec 3 700 euros net par mois, je ne peux même pas toucher le bas du marché »
lemonde.description: Quelque douze millions de personnes vivent seules dans leur logement en France, et leur nombre augmente régulièrement. Le parc résidentiel n’est pas adapté à cette évolution, amplifiant l’effet de la crise de l’immobilier sur ces ménages.

lemonde.title: Affaire Epstein : des parties civiles dénoncent la « lenteur » de la justice française et assignent l’Etat pour « faute lourde »
lemonde.description: L’association de protection de l’enfance Innocence en danger et la plaignante suédoise Ebba Karlsson soulignent les manquements de l’institution judiciaire, du fait des délais de traitement des accusations et des pistes d’enquête non suivies.

lemonde.title: Yann Vézilier, l’agent de la DGSE condamné au Mali à vingt ans de prison, a été gracié
lemonde.description: Après un an de détention, Yann Vézilier, qui était dûment accrédité comme officier de la direction générale de la sécurité extérieure auprès des autorités maliennes, a été gracié jeudi par le chef de la junte, le général Assimi Goïta. Une libération obtenue au terme de plusieurs mois de tractations diplomatiques.

lemonde.title: La plateforme des impôts victime d’une cyberattaque
lemonde.description: Bercy confirme que le système d’information du fisc a été victime fin juin d’un « accès illégitime », permettant « la consultation et l’extraction de données concernant des particuliers et des professionnels ».

lemonde.title: « Sa fonction de directeur l’oblige à faire un discours. Il me regarde à peine » : le pot de départ sans saveur de Cerise, cadre en école d’ingénieurs
lemonde.description: « Bon vent ! » (10/18). Un discours aussi court qu’humiliant de la part de son supérieur : c’est ce qu’a dû subir Cerise, 52 ans, responsable de filière dans une école d’ingénieurs.

lemonde.title: Championnats d’Europe de natation 2026 : Maxime Grousset, médaillé d’argent sur 100 m papillon, prend sa « revanche émotionnelle » sur Paris 2024
lemonde.description: Deux ans après des Jeux décevants sur le plan individuel, le nageur français s’est offert une troisième médaille, jeudi, devant le public du Centre aquatique de Saint-Denis. Quelques minutes plus tard, Mary-Ambre Moluh s’est offert l’argent sur 50 m dos.

lemonde.title: Le Sénégal et la Gambie redéfinissent leurs frontières communes, héritées de la colonisation
lemonde.description: Le 29 juillet, un accord définitif a été finalisé pour clarifier le tracé des 749 kilomètres de frontière terrestre entre les deux pays, a annoncé le Secrétariat permanent sénégalo-gambien. Cette frontière avait été dessinée « sur une carte à main levée dans un huis clos parisien », le 10 août 1889.

lemonde.title: Les pompiers, « très déçus » après avoir rencontré Laurent Nuñez, appellent à une mobilisation d’ampleur fin septembre
lemonde.description: L’intersyndicale des pompiers prévoit « une manifestation statique » les 26, 27 et 28 septembre, place de la République à Paris, qui sera appelée « colonnes de la révolte », selon l’UNSA - Sapeurs-pompiers.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : la Russie affirme ne pas avoir reçu de « proposition formelle » pour un moratoire sur les attaques en mer Noire
lemonde.description: La semaine dernière, la Turquie avait réclamé à Moscou et à Kiev la mise en place d’un « moratoire » sur ces attaques en mer Noire, en réponse à la recrudescence de celles-ci. « Aucune paix ne peut être instaurée sans s’attaquer aux causes profondes du conflit. Tout cessez-le-feu sera utilisé par la partie ukrainienne pour se regrouper et renforcer ses forces », a insisté le vice-ministre des affaires étrangères russe.

lemonde.title: « C’était soit l’exil soit la prison » : rencontre avec Boris Nadejdine, l’opposant au Kremlin poursuivi à Moscou et réfugié à Paris depuis début août
lemonde.description: Le vétéran de la politique russe, âgé de 63 ans, a essayé de lutter contre le régime de Vladimir Poutine et sa guerre en Ukraine par les voies légales et électorales. En vain. Menacé d’arrestation, il s’est résolu à quitter la Russie. Il a accordé au « Monde » ses premiers mots depuis son arrivée en France.

lemonde.title: Soudan : Khartoum visée par des frappes de drones des paramilitaires pour le deuxième jour de suite
lemonde.description: Les paramilitaires des Forces de soutien rapide ont lancé mercredi une vaste attaque coordonnée de drones, visant la capitale et d’autres villes contrôlées par l’armée, distantes de plusieurs centaines de kilomètres.

lemonde.title: Ebola en RDC : l’épidémie s’étend à une sixième province et menace le Soudan du Sud
lemonde.description: Une personne est morte de la maladie dans la province du Bas-Uele (nord), frontalière de la République centrafricaine et jusqu’à présent épargnée.

lemonde.title: Les paiements par téléphone sont en forte hausse, mais l’argent liquide résiste
lemonde.description: Deux tiers des entreprises de la zone euro acceptent désormais les paiements par téléphone mobile, deux fois plus qu’en 2024.

lemonde.title: En Cisjordanie occupée, Israël inaugure la colonie de Ganim, démantelée en 2005
lemonde.description: Ganim est l’une des quatre colonies israéliennes évacuées par Israël dans le cadre du plan de retrait de l’ancien premier ministre Ariel Sharon en 2005, avec Homesh, Sa-Nur et Kadim, toutes situées dans le nord du territoire palestinien.

lemonde.title: « Tip Toe », sur HBO Max : l’homophobie, une folie meurtrière
lemonde.description: La nouvelle série de Russell T Davies prend acte du recul de la tolérance envers la communauté homosexuelle, à travers la cohabitation devenue impossible entre deux voisins, un patron de bar de gay et un électricien réac’.

france24fr.title: Canicules et sécheresse records: un été catastrophique en France et en Europe
france24fr.description: La vague de chaleur actuelle en France dure depuis 17 jours. Elle a dépassé en longueur celle de 2003. Cet été brûlant a aussi entraîné une sécheresse record en Europe. Au point que les fleuves européens sont à leur plus bas niveau. La Roumanie a dû mettre à l'arrêt son unique centrale nucléaire que le Danube ne pouvait plus refroidir. Le débit du Rhin perturbe le transport fluvial de marchandises. Et une commune de l'est de la France a dû être ravitaillée en eau par camion-citerne.

france24fr.title: Thierry Burkhard, l’ex-chef d’état-major des armées françaises, n’a jamais prononcé ces phrases
france24fr.description: Des internautes attribuent à tort des propos contre l’Ukraine ou critiques envers Emmanuel Macron à l’ancien chef d’état-major des armées françaises, le général Thierry Burkhard. Ces citations ont été inventées de toutes pièces et font partie d’une désinformation récurrente à l’encontre du général.

france24fr.title: La visite de Poutine aux îles Kouriles provoque la colère du Japon
france24fr.description: Jeudi 13 août 2026, Vladimir Poutine s’est rendu pour la première fois aux îles Kouriles, un archipel disputé avec le Japon depuis 1945. Une visite qui ravive les tensions entre Moscou et Tokyo, le Japon a déclaré avoir convoqué l’ambassadeur de Russie.

france24fr.title: Avec la sécheresse en France, 40 000 personnes face au risque de pénurie d'eau potable
france24fr.description: Alors qu'une nouvelle canicule s'étend jeudi sur l'Hexagone, des dizaines de communes sont contraintes de se ravitailler en eau potable par camion-citerne ou dons de bouteille tandis que 70 % du territoire fait l'objet de mesures de restrictions des usages en raison de la sécheresse. Certaines localités françaises pourraient-elles venir à manquer d'eau potable ? Éléments de réponse.

france24fr.title: Pologne : arrestation d'un ressortissant russe chargé d'"exécuter" un Américano-Ukrainien à Varsovie
france24fr.description: Un ressortissant russe qui aurait reçu "l'ordre" de Moscou d'"exécuter" un citoyen américano-ukrainien à Varsovie a été interpellé, a annoncé jeudi le Premier ministre polonais, Donald Tusk. L'assassinat a été empêché de justesse.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie : des colons israéliens maintiennent le siège de maisons palestiniennes
france24fr.description: Des colons israéliens maintiennent le blocus de plusieurs maisons palestiniennes dans le nord de la Cisjordanie occupée, malgré l'intervention de l'armée israélienne.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Mali : "grâce présidentielle" accordée à Yann Vézilier, un agent de la DGSE condamné à 20 ans de prison
Mali : "grâce présidentielle" accordée à un agent français de la DGSE condamné à 20 ans de prison
france24fr.description: Le chef de la junte malienne Assimi Goïta a gracié Yann Vézilier, un agent français de la DGSE condamné en juin au Mali à 20 ans de prison, selon un communiqué du gouvernement malien publié jeudi sur Facebook.

france24fr.title: Nigéria : le pari des véhicules électriques face à la crise du carburant
france24fr.description: À Lagos, le vrombissement des embouteillages pourrait-il laisser place au silence des véhicules électriques ? Face à la flambée des prix du carburant, certains automobilistes nigérians se tournent vers l’électrique. Mais dans le premier pays producteur de pétrole d’Afrique, la transition reste semée d’embûches.

france24fr.title: "On va droit dans le mur" : les pompiers appellent à la mobilisation fin septembre
france24fr.description: Les soldats du feu sont sortis jeudi "très déçus" de leur réunion avec le ministre de l'Intérieur Laurent Nuñez. Rassemblés en intersyndicale, ils lui ont réclamé plus de moyens pour faire face à un nombre accru de crises. Une journée de mobilisation est prévue le 29 septembre.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : deux cheminots tués dans une frappe russe contre un train de passagers
france24fr.description: Un conducteur de train et son assistant ont été tués dans une attaque de drone russe contre un train de passagers dans la région d'Odessa, dans le sud de l'Ukraine, a annoncé jeudi le directeur des chemins de fer nationaux ukrainiens.

france24fr.title: Poutine en visite sur une île revendiquée par le Japon, Tokyo proteste
france24fr.description: Vladimir ​Poutine s'est rendu à Iturup, une île revendiquée par le Japon située à l'extrémité méridionale de l'archipel des Kouriles, près de l'île ​japonaise d'Hokkaido, ont rapporté jeudi les médias russes, une visite qui provoque la colère du gouvernement japonais.

france24fr.title: Reconstruction d'Alep : la capitale économique de la Syrie renaît de ses cendres
france24fr.description: Alep, capitale économique de la Syrie, a été dévastée par les combats qui ont vu s'y opposer les forces rebelles et le régime entre 2012 et 2016. Le séisme de 2023 a également lourdement endommagé la vieille ville. Mais aujourd'hui, la reconstruction est en cours, notamment pour les monuments historiques de la ville.

france24fr.title: Madagascar : des députés du président déchu rallient le pouvoir en place
france24fr.description: 🇲🇬 À Madagascar, une nouvelle formation politique voit le jour. Elle réunit 80 députés issus de l’opposition, dont certains membres de l’IRMAR, le parti de l’ancien président Andry Rajoelina. Cette plateforme se veut un soutien du pouvoir en place.

france24fr.title: Eclipse : à Dakar, passionnés et curieux réunis la tête dans les nuages
france24fr.description: L’éclipse solaire partielle a été observée ce mercredi dans plusieurs pays africains. En Tunisie, le phénomène a atteint 59,06 % d’occultation à Tabarka, tandis qu’à Dakar et dans plusieurs régions du Sénégal, près de 37 % du disque solaire a été masqué. À Dakar, de nombreux curieux se sont rassemblés pour assister à ce spectacle céleste, entre émerveillement et enthousiasme.

france24fr.title: "Territoire oublié de l’État" : après le séisme en Colombie, le Choco face à ses vieilles blessures
france24fr.description: Le puissant séisme qui a frappé lundi l'ouest de la Colombie a fait ressurgir les fragilités du Choco, département pauvre et isolé de la côte Pacifique. Alors que les secours peinent à atteindre certaines communautés, habitants et responsables locaux redoutent qu'une fois l'urgence passée, la région ne retombe dans l'oubli.

france24fr.title: Maghreb : pourquoi la fécondité chute à des niveaux historiques
france24fr.description: Saïd n'a eu que deux enfants afin de leur assurer de bonnes conditions de vie. Kaouthar ne veut pas en avoir du tout pour préserver sa "quiétude". Contraintes économiques, changements sociétaux: Maroc, Algérie et Tunisie connaissent une baisse historique de la fécondité.

france24fr.title: REPLAY - Eclipse solaire sur l'Europe, le nord de l'Espagne plongé dans le noir total
france24fr.description: Point d'orgue de l'éclipse solaire qui étend son ombre mercredi sur une partie de l'Europe, le nord de l'Espagne a été plongé dans le noir en plein jour, lorsque la Lune a entièrement masqué le Soleil, au grand ravissement de millions de personnes émerveillées par ce rare spectacle.

zeit.title: Kriminalität: Toter in München - Polizei fahndet nach Verdächtigem
Sieben Hektar betroffen: Brand bei Plauen: Löscharbeiten dauern an
Berliner Volksbühne: Veranstaltung für Schwarze Jugendliche im »Volksbad« abgesagt
zeit.description: Vor der Berliner Volksbühne steht aktuell ein Schwimmbad – das »Volksbad«. Eine dort für Freitag geplante Veranstaltung eines rassismuskritischen Vereins wurde abgesagt.

zeit.title: Feuer im Harz: Waldbrand im Harz könnte Einsatzkräfte Tage beschäftigen
Desinformationskampagne aus Russland: MDR warnt vor gefälschten Videos und Desinformationskampagne
zeit.description: Vor der Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt hat der MDR vor gefälschten Videos, teils mit MDR-Logo, gewarnt. Hinter den versuchten Einflussnahmen soll Russland stehen.

zeit.title: Schwimm-EM: Deutsche Schwimmer ohne Medaille - Viele Chancen am Freitag
Democratic Socialists of America: Rot sehen
zeit.description: In den USA fordern die Democratic Socialists die Demokraten heraus. Die Erneuerung der Partei ist überfällig. Aber die Bewegung hat auch eine dunkle Seite.

zeit.title: Kommunalwahl in Niedersachsen: Panne vor der Wahl - 27.500 neue Stimmzettel nötig
Bundesstraße gesperrt: Risse in Wildbrücke: Land prüft Lösungen für den Verkehr
Gutes Weinjahr: Weinbauern erwarten weniger, aber »qualitativ hervorragenden« Wein
zeit.description: Der Weinbauverband in Deutschland rechnet mit einer geringeren Ernte. Doch wenn jetzt Regen die Trauben zur Reife bringt, könnte es einen Spitzenjahrgang geben.

zeit.title: Verkehr: Straßeneinbruch beeinträchtigt Verkehr im Leipziger Westen
KNDS-Fabrik: Schwere Explosion in deutsch-französischer Munitionsfabrik nahe Rom
zeit.description: Auf dem Gelände des deutsch-französischen Konzerns KNDS in der Nähe von Rom hat es eine heftige Explosion gegeben. Die Fabrik produziert Munition und Brennstoffe.

zeit.title: Künstliche Intelligenz: Agenten! Überall Agenten!
zeit.description: Bei Google geht KI-Spitzenpersonal. Bots ersetzen wohl den Menschen im Netz. Und: Mark Zuckerbergs trauriges Verständnis von einer besseren Zukunft. Der KI-Newsletter

zeit.title: Owen Ansah: Er gewann Bronze, bald könnte er es wieder verlieren
zeit.description: Hat Owen Ansah eine Dopingprobe verweigert? Im Fall des Sprinters geht es nicht nur um seine Karriere, sondern auch um die Frage, was man Sportlern zumuten kann.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Trumps zweite Amtszeit: Antisemitismus-Klage gegen Harvard abgewiesen
nzz.description: Donald Trump regiert zum zweiten Mal als amerikanischer Präsident – mit weitreichenden innen- und aussenpolitischen Folgen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Schweizer Schwimmer Noè Ponti gewinnt EM-Bronze über 100 Meter Schmetterling
nzz.description: Der 25-jährige Tessiner holt seine erste Medaille an den Europameisterschaften in Paris.

nzz.title: Unternehmer beunruhigt: Ist die Kriminalität in Genf eine Gefahr für den Wirtschaftsstandort?
nzz.description: Genf hat die meisten Polizisten der Schweiz, aber die zweitmeisten Straftaten. Das ist das Resultat einer Befragung der Stiftung für die Attraktivität des Kantons.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Ein Bündnis mit dem BSW wäre für die AfD ein Spiel mit dem Feuer
nzz.description: Das Bündnis Sahra Wagenknecht will der AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt beispringen – doch ihr Spitzenkandidat lehnt ab. Siegmunds Absage ist klüger, als es zunächst scheint.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Wasserknappheit zwingt St. Galler Gemeinde zur Badischliessung +++  1200 Personen aus Camping in Frankreich evakuiert
nzz.description: Wo ist es zurzeit besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Die neuesten Meldungen über Hitzerekorde, Dürren und Brände in Europa.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Eruption am Ätna: Die Eindrücke in Bildern
nzz.description: Seit Anfang August stösst der Ätna auf Sizilien wieder verstärkt Lava und Asche aus. Ein Blick auf die jüngste Eruptionsphase und ihre Folgen für die Region um Catania.

nzz.title: Ärzte, Spitäler, Apotheker kassieren 360 Millionen Franken an Medikamentenrabatten ein, die eigentlich den Patienten gehören
nzz.description: Medizinische Versorger handeln mit Pharmafirmen Vergünstigungen aus, liefern sie aber nicht den Krankenkassen ab. Das gilt in der Branche immer noch als Kavaliersdelikt, wie ein Bericht der Finanzkontrolle zeigt.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die Karikatur der Woche
nzz.description: Der Karikaturist Peter Gut kommentiert in seinen wöchentlichen Zeichnungen für die NZZ das Weltgeschehen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Ärzte bereichern sich illegal: Jetzt müssen die Krankenkassen in die Verantwortung
nzz.description: Hunderte von Millionen Franken landen in einem intransparenten Rabattsystem jedes Jahr in den Taschen von Medizinern – statt bei den Prämienzahlern. So kann es nicht weitergehen.

nzz.title: Schwimmer machen gefährlichen Fund in Zürcher Flussbad: Scharfe Handgranate nahe dem Ufer entdeckt
nzz.description: Am Donnerstagnachmittag haben Spezialisten der Schweizer Armee eine Handgranate aus der Limmat geborgen. Sie stammt aus dem Jugoslawienkrieg.

nzz.title: «Das Bild meiner toten Tochter verfolgt mich jede Minute meines Lebens»: Zwei junge Menschen sterben in einer Lawine – nun urteilt das Gericht wegen fahrlässiger Tötung
nzz.description: Im Bergsport ist das Restrisiko immer dabei. Das Regionalgericht in Thun muss entscheiden, ob die Tourenleiter den Unfall hätten verhindern müssen.

nzz.title: Vernichtende Umfrage über die integrative Schule: Die Hälfte der Schweizer Lehrer hält das inklusive Modell für gescheitert, weil es sie überlastet – und die Schüler schlechter macht
nzz.description: Gerade jene Pädagogen, die am meisten betroffen sind, äussern sich negativ zum Status quo. Der Lehrerverband hält noch am System fest, fordert aber mehr Geld.

nzz.title: Vertrauliche Notkredite: Liquiditätshilfen der SNB für Banken sollen künftig geheim sein – und damit ihr Stigma verlieren
nzz.description: Eine Bank gerät unter Druck und braucht dringend Liquidität von der Nationalbank. Bisher musste sie solche Hilfe sofort publik machen. Geht es nach dem finalen «Too big to fail»-Paket des Bundesrates, soll sie in Zukunft schweigen dürfen.

nzz.title: Erster Besuch auf den Kurilen: Putin verärgert den Nachbarn Japan
nzz.description: Mit seiner Reise auf die umstrittene Inselgruppe demonstriert der russische Präsident geopolitische Entschlossenheit. Dass Putin nach Monaten in Moskau wieder vermehrt die russische Provinz besucht, hat aber auch innenpolitische Gründe.

nzz.title: Albulalinie in Graubünden wegen Erdrutsch gesperrt
nzz.description: Der Zugverkehr mehrerer Linien der Rhätischen Bahn ist bis Freitagabend unterbrochen.

observador.title: 12.349 notificações de reações adversas a medicamentos
observador.description: Sistema Nacional de Farmacovigilância recebeu em 2025 mais 9,2% de notificações de reações adversas do que em 2024. Dos 12.349 casos registados, 59,1% foram classificados como graves.

observador.title: Detido nos Açores por crimes sexuais e posse de armas
observador.description: O suspeito de 60 anos praticou atos sexuais de relevo no interior da sua residência contra uma amiga da sua neta. A PJ encontrou e apreendeu duas armas de fogo, uma arma de ar comprimido e munições.

observador.title: Seguro promulga diploma sobre direitos na gravidez
observador.description: No entender dos médicos, o termo "violência obstétrica" não tem validação científica. A expressão foi substituída por "práticas inadequadas, desrespeitosas ou não consentidas pelas mulheres".

observador.title: Pericas vence no Gerês e sobe a terceiro na geral
observador.description: O ciclista espanhol completou a etapa em 03:48.32 horas, com o mesmo tempo de Nych e Guérin. No entanto, o gaulês continua no topo da classificação geral, com Nych e Pericas nos lugares seguintes.

observador.title: Alentejo 2030 disponibiliza 130 mil euros
observador.description: Concurso destina-se a "projetos que promovam a utilização de ferramentas e soluções digitais inovadoras para reforçar a atratividade, a sustentabilidade e a coesão dos territórios rurais".

observador.title: Juntas de Lisboa pedem mais segurança na cidade
observador.description: Bala perdida e tráfico de droga relançam debate sobre crime e perceções na cidade de Lisboa. Autarcas de freguesias do centro histórico da capital falam em "sentimento de insegurança real".

observador.title: PSP defende criminalização da venda de louro prensado
observador.description: Polícia já fez propostas de alteração para combater fenómeno de venda de produtos que simulam estupefacientes. Posição surge após incidente na Baixa. Avisam que fenómeno já não é novo.

observador.title: Mosquito que pode transmitir Dengue ou Zika em Guimarães
observador.description: O mosquito Aedes albopictus, ou mosquito-tigre-asiático, foi detetado em Guimarães. A presença deste mosquito, no entanto, não significa que exista transmissão de doença.

observador.title: Águia visita Escócia depois da goleada na Luz
observador.description: Depois da goleada caseira, o Benfica já está de olho no Aarhus, mas primeiro tem de visitar Edimburgo para fechar as contas diante do Hearts. Marco Silva mexe no onze. Siga aqui em direto.

observador.title: UE com mínimos históricos de eletricidade a carvão em 2025
observador.description: Em 2024 e 2025, a quota total de carvão esteve abaixo dos 10%. A importância do carvão tem vindo a diminuir, devido à eliminação progressiva do uso do carvão pelos países da UE.

observador.title: 4 detidos por sequestro, roubo e tráfico de droga em Lisboa
observador.description: Grupo revelou um "elevado grau de perigosidade social e um modus operandi especialmente violento e dissimulado", segundo a Polícia Judiciária. Os detidos tinham entre 25 e 36 anos.

observador.title: Tutela pede à PGR que investigue antissemitismo na UC
observador.description: Secretária de Estado soube do caso em maio. Frases como "Beware of Zionists" e "Yahya Sinwar was a hero" foram expostas e Universidade alega ter reportado às autoridades as queixas do estudante.

observador.title: Homem detido por abuso sexual de menor em Mafra
observador.description: O suspeito de 30 anos começou a ter comportamentos que "escalaram para atos sexuais de relevo, decorrendo ao longo de quase dois meses". A menor foi também vítima de violência física.

observador.title: Julho supera inverno em número de chamadas para o INEM
observador.description: Durante o mês de julho deste ano, foram atendidas, em média, 4.943 chamadas por dia e houve sete dias com mais de cinco mil chamadas diárias atendidas.

observador.title: Poiares. Empresários querem acesso direto a Zona Industrial
observador.description: Associação considera prioritária criação de nó de acesso direto ao IP3, determinante para atrair investimento para a região. Investimento deve assegurar resposta às necessidades do tecido empresarial.

observador.title: PCP quer apoios para levar decreto-lei da PSU ao Parlamento
observador.description: O partido comunista afirma que "intervirá para que seja feita a apreciação parlamentar do decreto-lei" atrav+és do apoio de outras bancadas. Afirmam que o decreto "enfraquece os direitos sociais".

observador.title: 18h. Greve de técnicos de emergência pré-hospitalar
observador.description: Em causa a nova lei orgânica do INEM, que prevê a passagem das ambulâncias do Instituto de Emergência Médica para as Unidades Locais de Saúde. Ainda, PSD e CDS querem ouvir Nuno Melo no Parlamento.

observador.title: Suspeito de abusar sexualmente de uma criança em preventiva
observador.description: O suspeito, amigo da família, aproveitou-se do ascendente e da relação de confiança que tinha sobre a criança. A investigação começou com uma denúncia da mãe da menor.

spiegel.title: Landkreis Leer: 27.500 fehlerhafte Stimmzettel müssen neu gedruckt werden
spiegel.description: Alle Namen da, aber kein Feld zum Ankreuzen: Vor den Kommunalwahlen in Niedersachsen müssen im Landkreis Leer Tausende fehlerhafte Stimmzettel ausgetauscht werden. Wer bereits per Briefwahl abgestimmt hat, kann unbesorgt sein.

spiegel.title: Wolfram Weimer - Streit über Verlagsförderung: Bekommt er letztlich seinen Willen?
spiegel.description: Als der Kulturstaatsminister linke Buchhandlungen in die Nähe von Verfassungsfeinden rückte, war die Aufregung groß. Nun glaubt die Branche, Wolfram Weimer eingefangen zu haben – und setzt auf einen schwierigen Kompromiss.

spiegel.title: Türkei: Feuer auf Ausflugsboot – mehrere Verletzte
spiegel.description: Beinahe endet die Schifffahrt vor der Küste des Badeorts Fethiye in einer Katastrophe: Flammen erfassen das ganze Boot, 115 Menschen retten sich ins Wasser. An Bord befanden sich offenbar viele Kinder.

spiegel.title: Kanye West und JD Sports: Wie kann es sein, dass dieser Mann noch Geschäftspartner findet?
spiegel.description: Kanye West wurde nach antisemitischen Ausfällen von Adidas vor die Tür gesetzt. Nun vertreibt die Sportmodekette JD Sports die Yeezy-Schuhlinie des Rappers in den USA. PR-Profi Eric Yaverbaum hält das für keine gute Idee.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Volksbühne sagt Veranstaltung exklusiv für Schwarze Menschen ab
spiegel.description: Einen Nachmittag lang sollte nur die Schwarze Community im Freibad vor der Volksbühne schwimmen dürfen. Politikerinnen von CDU und AfD äußerten Kritik, die Organisatoren berichten von Drohmails – und ziehen nun die Notbremse.

spiegel.title: KNDS: Explosion in Munitionsfabrik von deutsch-französischem Rüstungskonzern bei Rom
spiegel.description: Fernsehbilder zeigen eine große Rauchsäule und Rettungskräfte im Einsatz: In einer Munitionsfabrik des Rüstungskonzerns KNDS bei Rom ist es zu einer Explosion gekommen. Verletzt wurde ersten Angaben zufolge niemand.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: CDU-Kandidat Sven Schulze, zwei Wahlplakate und ein Fauxpas
spiegel.description: Spott und Häme für Sven Schulze, den Spitzenkandidaten der CDU in Sachsen-Anhalt: Zwei seiner Wahlplakate zeigen dieselbe »Frau aus dem Volk«, allerdings mal im Rollstuhl, mal nicht. Peinliche Panne oder gängige Praxis?

spiegel.title: Flaschenpost: Wie groß ist die Chance, dass sie heil ankommt und gefunden wird?
spiegel.description: Eine Flaschenpost kann versinken, verblassen oder an eine menschenleere Küste treiben: Trotzdem werden überraschend viele gefunden, mitunter nach mehr als 100 Jahren.

spiegel.title: Erykah Badu: Erstes Studioalbum seit 16 Jahren mit The Alchemist als Produzenten
spiegel.description: Sie gilt als die »Queen of Neo-Soul«, doch in den vergangenen Jahren war auf Tonträgern nur sporadisch von Erykah Badu zu hören. Dafür half sie bei Geburten. Jetzt kommt neue Musik – und in zwei Wochen sogar ein Album.

spiegel.title: Karoline Leavitt: Angriffslustige Trump-Sprecherin beendet ihre Zeit im Weißen Haus
spiegel.description: Sie war die jüngste Regierungssprecherin in der Geschichte der USA – und vor allem bekannt für ihre angriffslustige Rhetorik gegenüber Journalisten. Die einprägsamsten Szenen im Video.

spiegel.title: Israel: US-Botschafter Mike Huckabee nennt Siedlergewalt im Westjordanland »Terrorakt«
spiegel.description: Tagelang hatten Siedler das Zuhause einer Familie im Westjordanland blockiert. Sonst eher unkritisch eingestellt, findet der US-Botschafter Huckabee jetzt scharfe Worte.

spiegel.title: Dänemark – Ålbæk: Seltener Riesenhai am Kattegat angeschwemmt
spiegel.description: Riesenhaie sind namensbedingt zutiefst missverstandene Tiere. An der dänischen Küste ist jetzt ein totes Exemplar aufgefunden worden. Die zuständige Biologin zeigt sich begeistert.

spiegel.title: Afghanistan: Taliban lassen sechs Menschenrechtler gewaltsam verschwinden
spiegel.description: Seit fünf Jahren regieren die Taliban das Land, immer verschleppen sie Mitarbeitende von Hilfsorganisationen in Afghanistan. Human Rights Watch ist nach einem neuen Fall alarmiert.

spiegel.title: Nicole Kidman geht auf Ibiza raven – mit Sonnenbrille und Perücke
spiegel.description: Nicole Kidman verbringt den Sommer nach ihrer Scheidung von Keith Urban in Europa. Auf Ibiza verbringt sie die Abende mit einer gemütlichen Partie Scrabble – oder sie zieht in den Club.

spiegel.title: »James Webb«-Teleskop: Extrem heller Punkt könnte Schwarzes-Loch-Stern sein
spiegel.description: Aufnahmen des »James Webb«-Teleskops zeigen immer wieder rätselhafte rote Punkte. Nun haben Forschende eine bislang unbekannte Art von Objekten entdeckt, die eine mögliche Erklärung liefern könnte.

spiegel.title: Ebola-Ausbruch: Mehr als 2000 Todesfälle in der Demokratischen Republik Kongo
spiegel.description: Alle 30 Minuten stirbt im Kongo ein Mensch an Ebola, nie zuvor hat sich das Virus so schnell ausgebreitet. Es ist den Ärzten weit voraus, die in dem Kriegsgebiet auch noch bedroht werden. Die Uno ruft die Welt zu Hilfe.

spiegel.title: USA: Sitzen bald 2000 Gamer als Fluglotsen im Tower?
spiegel.description: Den USA fehlen Fluglotsen. Um die Lücke zu füllen, hat der US-Verkehrsminister eine Kampagne gestartet, mit der 2000 Gamer für den Beruf gewonnen wurden. Doch es gibt Sicherheitsbedenken.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Dürre in der Landwirtschaft, Ebola in Afrika, Zhu Rongji
spiegel.description: In Deutschland wird das Heu knapp, in der Demokratischen Republik Kongo wütet Ebola, und in Peking wird der Mann betrauert, der Chinas Wirtschaftskraft entfesselt hat. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagabend.

letemps.title: Basil Da Cunha retrouve la compétition du Locarno Film Festival avec «O Jacaré», un film qui célèbre le pouvoir de la fiction
letemps.description:

phys-org.title: India faces rising uncompensable heat stress, especially during monsoon season
phys-org.description: Animals struggle to cool down in extreme heat and high humidity, and heat stress is rising in many regions around the world. This is especially true for people in tropical countries, including populous India. In a new paper in AGU Advances, researchers characterize the extent of India's "uncompensable heat stress" and project how the problem could worsen in the future.

phys-org.title: How multilayer nanocoatings dissipate energy at the nanoscale to prevent failure
phys-org.description: An international research team including Alexander Korsunsky from the Skoltech Engineering Center has, for the first time, directly measured mechanical stresses at the contact between a diamond indenter and a complex nanostructured coating at a resolution of less than 80 nanometers.

phys-org.title: Millions of Europeans struggle with another wave of extreme heat
phys-org.description: Millions of people across Europe—particularly in France, Italy, Spain and the UK—sweltered through another wave of extreme temperatures Thursday as the continent's latest heat wave intensified.

phys-org.title: Review of studies on single-use plastics reveals broader circular economy approach is needed
phys-org.description: A review of research published in the Interdisciplinary Environmental Review on single-use plastics argues that tackling the waste problem will require a shift from recycling alone to a broader circular economy approach, in which materials are kept in use through reuse, recovery, recycling and redesign.

phys-org.title: Paleontologists reconstruct forests of 56 million years ago with chilling parallels for our warming planet
phys-org.description: If you want to know how rapidly pumping carbon dioxide into the atmosphere will affect future forest ecosystems, you have to look into the distant past. The researchers behind a new study published in Science have done just that, reconstructing the forest canopy of 56 million years ago, during a massive and abrupt emission of carbon into the atmosphere during the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum (PETM). phys-org.title: Climate change decided who ruled as top predator 35 million years ago
phys-org.description: An international team of researchers from Belgium, France, Switzerland, Spain and the U.S. has reconstructed the evolution of body mass in carnivorous mammals during the Paleogene—a crucial window in the diversification of mammals that followed the extinction of dinosaurs. This work, published in Biology Letters, challenges the long-standing hypothesis that competition decided the fate of ancient top predators.

phys-org.title: GPS tracking study reveals why invasive barred owls are winning the battle for California's old-growth forests
phys-org.description: Newly published research offers some of the clearest evidence yet of why the invasive barred owl has become one of the greatest threats to the northern spotted owl and delivers encouraging evidence that managing barred owl populations can restore old-growth habitat for spotted owl recovery.

phys-org.title: Soft-bodied sea slug reconfigures anatomy to simplify feeding control
phys-org.description: Made entirely of muscle, with no rigid skeleton, muscular hydrostats like octopus arms, elephant trunks and human tongues can move in ways traditional mechanical systems cannot. Between crawling across the seafloor, picking up a peanut and enabling speech, scientists have long wondered how soft structures can perform so many different functions without becoming impossible to control.

phys-org.title: New research explores how home languages can strengthen early English reading instruction
phys-org.description: During a reading lesson, Mateo, an elementary multilingual learner (MLL) in a Delaware public school, read "sit" as "seat." Jon Kittle, his reading interventionist, walked him through the short vowel sound, but Mateo made the same "mistake" and grew frustrated. Kittle began to wonder if these "errors" were actually the result of Mateo applying what he knew from Spanish, where the letter "i" carries the sound of the English long "ē."

phys-org.description: Like a delivery driver navigating crowded city streets, a gene-therapy-toting lipid nanoparticle faces a gauntlet of potential detours on its journey toward a cell's nucleus. phys-org.title: Robinhood users target simplicity in choosing stocks
phys-org.description: Millions of investors using the Robinhood app tend to favor simpler, easy-to-understand stocks, according to new research from Washington State University—and those stocks outperformed more complex firms during the study period.

phys-org.title: A new category of heat waves is melting western US snowpack faster
phys-org.description: Heat waves are not all created equal. While some bring dry heat that rapidly dries out crops, others carry a lot of moisture that can prevent sweat from evaporating off the skin. In new research published in the journal Science Advances, scientists have identified another type of heat wave that they call a "snow-eater."

phys-org.title: College men's attitudes linked to ignoring rejections from bisexual women
phys-org.description: Alexis Sheffield, a doctoral candidate in clinical psychology, recently published a research article about a study exploring factors that contribute to the elevated rates of sexual assault among bisexual women and to better understand that disparity.

phys-org.title: Journalism is key to combating bad practices in science
phys-org.description: Watchdog science journalism has become a fundamental tool to counter scientific malpractice, such as publication fraud, abuse and political and corporate manipulation of science. A study by the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB) has mapped for the first time the rise of this type of journalism in Ibero-America through interviews with 15 journalists from the region who have investigated prominent cases of bad science. phys-org.title: New fiber-based electronic device generates power and detects harmful gas
phys-org.description: Research teams have developed a multifunctional fiber-shaped electronic device capable of both generating electricity and detecting hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) gas. The achievement demonstrates that a single fiber can function as a self-powered safety sensor that generates its own electricity while detecting hazardous gases. phys-org.title: Indigenous land restitution empowers communities, but environmental gains require extra support
phys-org.description: Charting a better future will require redressing the problems of the past. That's one reason many countries have begun to return dispossessed land to Indigenous peoples. The goal of Indigenous land restitution is to empower disadvantaged communities and entrust land management back to the region's traditional stewards. In many cases, these programs also carry expectations of broad environmental benefits. However, there's been relatively little research testing this assumption.

phys-org.title: Fishing nets main cause of death among Cornwall's stranded common dolphins
phys-org.description: Fishing nets remain the most common cause of death among common dolphins that strand on Cornwall's coast, new research shows.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: The Real Competitiveness Test
proj-syn.description: The balance of global investment has shifted dramatically over the past three decades, with China emerging as the leading destination for productive capital. Europe and the United States can still narrow the gap, but only by making it cheaper and easier to build, operate, and innovate.

proj-syn.title: Our AI, Your Problem
proj-syn.description: The debate over whether European firms should use a Chinese state-directed model or one built by a private US firm threatens to distract from Europe’s most pressing problem, which is that it has no seat at either table. To preserve its own sovereignty, the continent must create a third option for itself.

proj-syn.title: Chile’s Boring Conservative President
proj-syn.description: Rather than governing like a pugnacious populist or a ruthless pragmatist, Chile’s new president, José Antonio Kast, has adopted an old-school center-right agenda and governing style reminiscent of the 1980s. Yet even this potentially safer approach comes with its own risks and costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe Failed the Ceuta Test
proj-syn.description: The current migration crisis is eating away at the solidarity on which the European Union depends, fueling the rise of the far right and pushing leaders to adopt increasingly hardline policies. But the Ceuta debacle shows why such measures cannot address the deeper forces driving migration.

proj-syn.title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
proj-syn.description: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics. Once there, he implemented many of the reforms that turned the country into an economic powerhouse.

proj-syn.title: The Twilight of the ICC
proj-syn.description: Born amid the euphoria of the West’s Cold War victory, the International Criminal Court embodied the aspiration that international law could transcend politics. But the ICC always represented victors’ justice, and it was never equipped to operate in a world shaped by Machtpolitik.

proj-syn.title: Will Latin America Embrace Guerrilla Geopolitics?
proj-syn.description: The resurgence of guerrilla warfare in Ukraine and Iran has underscored the potential benefits of asymmetric action in today’s increasingly multipolar world. Latin America, in particular, should consider how to leverage its many strengths to remedy its relatively weak position on the global stage.

proj-syn.title: China’s Biggest Weakness on AI
proj-syn.description: When a state can credibly promise that labor displacement will not mean destitution, workers and their representatives are more likely to accept technological change. But since China can promise no such thing, its lack of a robust welfare state has emerged as a fundamental weakness in the broader AI race.

proj-syn.title: The Monetary Roots of Political Extremism
proj-syn.description: While the global economy generates unprecedented wealth for plutocrats like Elon Musk, it is, by design, highly unequal, dangerously over-indebted, prone to recurring financial crises, and ecologically disastrous. In such a context, radical reforms will be needed, beginning with the rejection of money as a commodity.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the Power Trust
proj-syn.description: A century ago, the US power industry was dominated by sprawling, heavily indebted holding companies until their collapse forced the federal government to break them up. Now, the pattern is repeating, with mega-mergers and buyouts advancing a debt-heavy business model at the expense of households and communities.

proj-syn.title: Morocco’s Bet on Targeted AI
proj-syn.description: Rather than join the global race for computing power, Morocco has focused on building sovereignty over its data, talent, and uses of AI, because technological power will be measured by usefulness, not by domination. This strategy calls for the country to embrace innovation without ceding its identity to foreign models.

proj-syn.title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
proj-syn.description: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

proj-syn.title: The Rise of the Token Economy
proj-syn.description: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.

proj-syn.title: Excess Savings Are Driving the New China Shock
proj-syn.description: The current China shock combines continued supply upgrading with an absorption problem: the decline in property and related investment has reduced domestic demand, but national saving remains very high. The result is a larger savings-investment surplus that spills into net exports.

proj-syn.title: The World Economy Is Swerving, and the Destination Is Unknown
proj-syn.description: The days of unfettered globalization, multilateral rule of law, commonly accepted limits on economic statecraft, and widely shared macroeconomic objectives are now long gone. A perpetual, directionless transition is our new reality, and corporate executives, investors, and policymakers must adapt accordingly.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Beggar-thy-Neighbor Power?
proj-syn.description: When major economies are running at near full capacity, it is not clear that trade deficits should be a cause for concern, since they represent a transfer of purchasing power from surplus countries. Under the current circumstances, then, China’s widely criticized surpluses might as well be called enrich-thy-neighbor.

proj-syn.title: No Escape from the Russian Terror Playbook
proj-syn.description: When Vladimir Putin revives Stalin-era repression tactics, he does not do so in service of some lofty ideology or grand project. Rather, he and his security apparatus are seeking to safeguard their own power indefinitely—and, as Russians well know, they will stop at nothing to succeed.

proj-syn.title: The Extractive Trap Has a Green Exit
proj-syn.description: For resource-rich developing countries, decades of resource extraction have produced income concentration, economic dependency, external vulnerabilities, and the weakening of other productive sectors. Achieving broad-based prosperity requires a new approach, one which leverages South-South cooperation to build green industries.
